items.title: Santo Pecora Interview, 1972-11-09
items.q: And that's what happened with Lawrence Welch, see. He couldn't sit in the band and read the charts, see. So, that's... And Lawrence Welch said, look, I'm a... I got five, six saxophone players. They'll teach you how to play, read music. So he didn't want it that way.

ctx.x: I had time to talk to him. God. I didn't get to talk to him either. He's had some operations and

everything. Yeah. Well, George is only a jobbing lately, you know. You see, George never played with bands like I did, you know. He played with Ted Lewis, you know, one of those things. But at that time, Dick, you didn't have to know how to read music or nothing. They were fakers, see. In fact, a lot of good jazz musicians, or good musicians, they can't read music. But still, they can't get a job with big bands because they have to read the charts. Well, he couldn't play shows. You see, you can't play shows or…

I gave it up. I had to quit. Yeah. What about playing a silent movie? What would that be like? Would you have to read much to do that? Oh. What a new movie would come up like? How would you play it? How did you know what to do?
